note: The 1901 census for Lenton Avenue, numbers 5 to 31 and 10 to 14, transcribed by A. Hagues from the enumerator's pages. Surnames are filled in from the head of household wherever the relationship column makes it certain — wife, son, daughter, and children entered under ditto marks — and are left alone for servants, boarders and visitors, who carry their own. Birthplaces are given in full: county abbreviations expanded, and New Radford written as Radford, Nottingham. Numbers 2, 4, 6 and 8 are deliberately absent: the Thompson, Blythe, Sims and Elmore households went in from an earlier file and would only double up. Two houses are entered by name with no number — Clumber Lodge, which falls between 17 and 21 in the enumerator's round, and Newlands, which falls after 31 — so they are left unfiled for a decision rather than guessed onto a number. Entries that collided with somebody the record already held under a fuller forename — Alice May Parr against Alice Mary, Constance Marjorie Smith against Constance M. — now carry that person's number. The importer matches names letter for letter and was making a second record of each of them on every run; a number matches whatever the spelling, survives a merge, and cannot mint a new person.
source: 1901 census, Lenton Avenue — transcribed by A. Hagues
